The Boston Celtics are an American professional basketball team based in Boston.
The Celtics compete in the National Basketball Association (NBA) as a member of the Atlantic Division of the Eastern Conference.
Founded in 1946, the Celtics were one of the league's original eight teams.
The Celtics play their home games at TD Garden, which is shared with the NHL's Boston Bruins.
The team is commonly regarded as the most successful in NBA history and holds records for the most NBA championships won (18) and most recorded wins of any NBA franchise.
The Celtics' rise to dominance began in the late 1950s under coach Red Auerbach, after acquiring Bill Russell in 1956.
Bill Russell, along with Bob Cousy, Tom Heinsohn, Don Nelson, K. C. Jones, John Havlicek, Sam Jones, Satch Sanders, and Bill Sharman, formed the core of the Celtics dynasty from 1959 to 1966.
After Red Auerbach retired as coach in 1966, Russell became player-coach and won back-to-back titles in 1968 and 1969.
The team entered a period of rebuilding after Bill Russell retired in 1969.
In the mid-1970s, under head coach Tom Heinsohn, the Celtics won championships in 1974 and 1976 with Dave Cowens, John Havlicek, and Jo Jo White leading the team.
The 1980s saw the Celtics return to dominance. Led by "Big Three" of Larry Bird, Kevin McHale, and Robert Parish, they won championships in 1981, 1984, and 1986 against the Lakers.
After the retirements of Larry Bird, Kevin McHale, and Robert Parish, as well as the untimely deaths of Len Bias and Reggie Lewis, the Celtics struggled through the 1990s and much of the early 2000s.
In 2007, under head coach Doc Rivers, the Celtics won their 17th championship by defeating the Lakers in the NBA Finals.
The "Celtics" nickname is a nod to Boston's historically large Irish population and also refers to the Original Celtics, a barnstorming basketball team from the early 20th century.
The Celtics have a notable rivalry with the Los Angeles Lakers, who are second in NBA history with 17 championships.
The teams' rivalry was especially pronounced in the 1960s and 1980s.
The Celtics have played the Lakers a record 12 times in the NBA Finals, winning nine of those series.

The Boston Celtics were formed on June 6, 1946, by Walter A. Brown.
In 1948, the team earned its first playoff appearance but lost to the Chicago Stags in a 4–1 series.
In 1949, the team missed the playoffs and finished fifth in the Eastern Division.
On August 3, 1949, the team became part of the National Basketball Association (NBA) following the merger of the BAA and rival NBL.
The Celtics signed Chuck Cooper in 1950, becoming the first NBA franchise to draft a black player.
Chuck Connors was an original member of the Celtics in 1946.
Bob Cousy played 13 years for the team, with 6 ending in NBA titles.
Red Auerbach initially refused to draft Bob Cousy out of Holy Cross because he was "too flashy."
After the 1955–56 season, Red Auerbach made a stunning trade by sending Ed Macauley to the St. Louis Hawks and Cliff Hagan's draft rights for the second overall pick.
Auerbach used the second overall pick to select Bill Russell from the University of San Francisco.
Auerbach also acquired Tom Heinsohn from Holy Cross, who was named NBA Rookie of the Year in 1957.
Bill Russell and Tom Heinsohn worked well with Bob Cousy and were key players for Auerbach's champion Celtics.
Following the acquisition of K.C. Jones in 1958, the Celtics began a dynasty that lasted more than a decade.
In 1959, the Celtics won their first NBA championship after sweeping the Minneapolis Lakers.
During this time, the Celtics met the Lakers in the Finals five times and formed an intense rivalry.
In 1964, the Celtics became the first NBA team to have an all-African-American starting lineup.
On December 26, 1964, Willie Naulls replaced Tom Heinsohn as a starter for the Celtics.
The Celtics won their next 11 games with Naulls in the starting lineup.
Auerbach retired as coach after the 1965–66 season and Russell took over as player-coach, which was Auerbach's strategy to keep Russell interested.
With his appointment, Russell became the first African-American coach in any U.S. pro sport.
The Celtics' string of NBA titles ended when they lost to the Philadelphia 76ers in the 1967 Eastern Conference Finals.
The team managed two more championships in 1968 and 1969 by defeating the Los Angeles Lakers each time.
Russell retired after the 1969 season, effectively ending a Celtics dynasty that had garnered an unrivaled 11 NBA titles in 13 seasons.
The 1969–70 season was a rebuilding year for the Celtics as they had their first losing record since 1949–50.
With the acquisition of Paul Silas and future Hall of Famers Dave Cowens and Jo Jo White, the Celtics soon became dominant again.
After losing in the Eastern Conference Finals in 1972, the Celtics regrouped and came out determined in 1973 with an excellent regular season record of 68–14.
However, they were upset by the New York Knicks in the Conference Finals.
The Celtics returned to the playoffs the next year, defeating the Milwaukee Bucks in the 1974 NBA Finals for their 12th championship.
Larry Bird played in the Celtics from 1979 to 1992 and is widely regarded as one of the greatest basketball players of all time.
Larry Bird debuted for the Celtics during the 1979–80 season.

The rivalry between the Boston Celtics and Los Angeles Lakers is considered the best in NBA history. They have met a record 12 times in the NBA Finals.
The Celtics have won the first eight finals meetings against the Lakers, while the Lakers have won three of the last four.
The rivalry with the Atlanta Hawks has lasted for over five decades.
The Boston Celtics and New York Knicks are rivals due to their location in the Atlantic division. They have played 512 regular-season games, with the Celtics winning 276 times.

The rivalry between the Celtics and the Philadelphia 76ers peaked in the 1980s when players such as Larry Bird, Kevin McHale, Robert Parish, Isiah Thomas, Bill Laimbeer, Dennis Rodman, and Joe Dumars were on the teams. They met in the NBA playoffs five times from 1985 to 1991.
The rivalry between the Celtics and the Washington Wizards intensified during the 2015–16 season due to incidents involving Jae Crowder and Al Horford.
The Boston Celtics logo features a leprechaun spinning a basketball, named Lucky. It was originally designed by Zang Auerbach.
Through the 1995–96 season, the logo's only colors were green, white, and black.
For the 1996–97 season, celebrating the club's 50th anniversary, the logo got a full-color treatment with Lucky's face and hands painted tan, while gold was included on the vest, bow tie, and hat.

The primary uniforms have seen minimal changes since the 1950s.
The green uniforms feature either the city name or the team name on the front.
When Nike became the NBA's uniform provider in 2017, they eliminated "home" and "away" designations, renaming them "Icon" and "Association" uniforms.
From 2005 to 2017, the Celtics wore alternate green uniforms with black lettering and trim featuring the word "Boston."
A gray uniform set was also used from 2014 to 2017, dubbed "Parquet Pride."
Between 2006 and 2017, the Celtics wore special St. Patrick's Day uniforms.
During the NBA Europe Live Tour prior to the 2007–08 season, they used alternate road jerseys with a patch containing the Union Jack.
The team has honored deceased members of the Celtics family with a commemorative black band on the left shoulder strap of the jersey.
